scientific.claim: Let \(\mathcal H\) be a nonzero finite-dimensional real or complex Hilbert space and let \(\Omega\) be an infinite set. For every unit-vector family \(\{\tau_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\Omega}\subset\mathcal H\), one has \[\sup_{\alpha\ne\beta}|\langle\tau_\alpha,\tau_\beta\rangle|=1.\] If \(\mathcal H\) is real, then also \(\sup_{\alpha\ne\beta}\langle\tau_\alpha,\tau_\beta\rangle=1\). Consequently, under Definition 3.7 of arXiv:2109.09296v1, every normalized continuous frame on an infinite index set has continuous frame correlation exactly \(1\); whenever such frames exist, every one of them is a continuous Grassmannian frame in Definition 3.8 and the defining infimum equals \(1\). In particular, if \(0<\mu(\Omega)<\infty\) and \(\mu\) is nonatomic, then for every integer \(d\ge1\) there is a normalized tight continuous frame for \(\mathbb K^d\), obtained from an equal-measure measurable \(d\)-partition, and all normalized continuous frames on that measure space are continuous Grassmannian in the published sense. For finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces, the signed supremum used in the continuous Rankin optimization of arXiv:2311.07606v1 is likewise identically \(1\) on every infinite index set.
scientific.integrity: The proof is a direct compactness argument. No numerical experiment, unpublished certificate, or inaccessible result is used as a correctness premise. The primary source statements and the closest related continuous Rankin formulation were materially inspected; an unindexed folklore observation remains a residual originality risk.
scientific.limitations: The theorem concerns finite-dimensional nonzero Hilbert spaces and infinite index sets. It does not apply to finite index sets or infinite-dimensional spaces, and it does not trivialize integral frame potentials or RMS-type correlations. The nonatomic construction proves existence only for finite positive nonatomic measure spaces, not for arbitrary measures.

title: Infinite-index continuous Grassmannian correlation is identically one
